assertions.name: gmor_lo_reproduces_squared_ratio_within_chpt_lo
assertions.unit: relative gap, GMOR LO vs m_K²/m_π²
assertions.source: Route A: (m_K/m_π)² from PDG-2024 charged meson masses. Route B: (m_u+m_s)/(m_u+m_d) from PDG MS-bar quark masses at 2 GeV — disjoint inputs. Bound 15% = the LO-χPT gap NLO closes; the same GMOR value misses the LINEAR ratio by 296%, which is the reframe this replaces a narration flag with.

assertions.name: sweep_winner_is_the_spin1_spin3half_fusion_sum
assertions.source: Route A: the sweep winner, chosen by proximity to the measured m_K²/m_π². Route B: the fusion sum [2]_q+[4]_q+[6]_q. The winner this run is [4]_q·[3]_q.

description: Tests derived routes for m_K/m_π via GMOR (squared ratio) and pure q-integer forms. Best m_K²/m_π² candidate: [4]_q·[3]_q at 0.02% miss. GMOR reframes the target as the squared ratio (m_u+m_s)/(m_u+m_d), correcting the 71% linear-ratio artifact.
caveats: The (a) candidate list declares 11 forms but only 10 distinct ones: '[5]_q²/[2]_q' and '[5]_q·[5]_q/[2]_q' are the same expression, so that value is scored twice. Recorded, not repaired — it does not change the winner ([4]_q·[3]_q) or any number here.

best_pure_q_miss_pct and mK2_mpi2_eq_3q4q_miss_ppm drift ~4.5e-5 relative between container images (python/numpy/scipy versions) with no source change. Environmental; the assertions above are stated against bounds far wider than that drift.
